shots.vo: In Indonesia, if you hear a woman laughing far away…
RUN.
She's called Kuntilanak.

shots.camera: Slow dolly back, fade to mist
shots.vo: A woman who died before her baby was born.
She waits in tall trees… and before she comes, you smell frangipani.
My grandmother taught me the rule.
If her laugh sounds far… she's close. If it sounds close… she's far.
One night, I walked home alone… through the banana trees.
Then I heard it. Laughing. Far away.
I didn't think. I ran.
Then it came again. Right next to my ear.
I almost smiled. Close means far. I was safe.

shots.camera: Static, rack focus front to back
shots.vo: But then I heard it far… and close…

shots.camera: Push to eyes, fade to black
shots.vo: …at the same time. Grandma never told me what that means.
Now… listen. Is she laughing near you… or far?
Comment NEAR or FAR
On Java's southern coast, there's one rule.

shots.camera: Green fabric whips across frame, hard stop
shots.vo: Never wear green.
The sea belongs to Nyi Roro Kidul, Queen of the Southern Sea.
Green is her color. Wear it, and she thinks you're calling her.
A hotel by that beach still keeps one room for her.
Room 308.
My mother packed my bag herself.

shots.camera: Hands pull out a green scarf, set it aside
shots.vo: No green. She checked twice.
At sunset, the sea pulled back. Far back.
Everyone took photos.
I walked closer.
A wave touched my feet. Just foam.
I laughed.

Comment your shirt color.

shots.hero: Title 'POCONG' + 'An Indonesian legend' over a shrouded silhouette

shots.hero: A shrouded body lying on a mat, three ties (head, waist, feet) clearly drawn

shots.framing: Tracking side view, riding at night

shots.framing: Medium from behind at a red light
shots.hero: Uncle's back + the white cloth wrapped around his waist, red light glow
shots.vo: At a red light, he looked down at her arms around his waist.

shots.hero: White shroud cloth around the jacket, ending in a tied knot instead of hands

shots.framing: Close on the uncle's helmet and ear
shots.hero: Helmet edge and ear in profile, a pale cloth edge appearing behind
shots.vo: Then, right behind his ear…

shots.framing: Extreme close, the pale cloth face

shots.vo: Untie me.

shots.hero: Motorbike parked alone at dawn; a few white threads on the seat
shots.vo: He rode until sunrise without looking back. The seat behind him was empty. But it was still cold.

shots.framing: Wide, cemetery gate at night again
shots.hero: The white figure under the street light again, slightly closer to the road
shots.vo: She still waits by that cemetery. For the next ride.

shots.hero: CTA type with a knotted cloth motif

shots.hero: A distant train headlight in the dark tunnel mouth, tracks gleaming
shots.vo: In Jakarta, if the last train arrives with every light on… and no sound… don't get on.

shots.hero: Title 'THE GHOST TRAIN' + 'Kereta Hantu · Jakarta' over a glowing train front
shots.vo: They call it the ghost train.

shots.hero: A split-flap / LED departure board: last line flickers to a blank row with a red dot
shots.vo: It comes after the final departure. A train that isn't on any schedule.

shots.hero: Rows of identical pale passengers all facing the doors; one empty seat lit
shots.vo: Inside, the passengers don't move. They're waiting… for one more.

shots.framing: Medium, narrator alone on a bench
shots.hero: Narrator silhouette with backpack on a bench under one lamp; clock showing 00:40

shots.hero: The bright train sliding into the station, windows glowing, no motion blur needed

shots.framing: Medium, doors opening in front of the narrator

shots.hero: A wall of identical pale faces in rows, all eyes on camera

shots.framing: Medium, guard pulling the narrator back
shots.hero: Guard's gloved hand on the narrator's shoulder, cap silhouette, vest stripe catching light

shots.framing: Close on the guard, half in shadow

shots.framing: Wide, the train leaving into the dark

shots.hero: Empty platform; on the bench, a guard's cap left behind

shots.hero: CTA with a red signal light motif

shots.hero: Long corridor, flickering light at the end, a white shape low on the floor far away
shots.vo: In Indonesian hospitals, if you hear something dragging across the floor at night… don't look under your bed.

shots.hero: Title 'SUSTER NGESOT' + 'The crawling nurse' with a nurse's cap silhouette
shots.vo: They call her Suster Ngesot. The crawling nurse.

shots.hero: An old nurse's cap and a clipboard on the floor tiles, a long hair strand
shots.vo: A nurse who died in this hospital. She still does her night rounds… on the floor.

shots.framing: Wide, the ward with beds and curtains
shots.hero: Row of beds with curtains; a low shadow moving along the floor between them
shots.vo: Patients say she checks every bed. Every single night.

shots.hero: Narrator on a plastic chair beside the bed, grandma asleep, IV stand, monitor glow

shots.hero: Fluorescent tubes stuttering; a dark trail appearing on the floor toward the bed

shots.framing: Low angle, floor under the narrator's chair
shots.hero: Chair legs and the narrator's sneakers; in the dark under the chair, pale fingertips on the tiles
shots.vo: It stopped… right under my chair.

shots.framing: Close, grandma's hand gripping the narrator's

shots.vo: Grandma opened her eyes and whispered…

shots.framing: Close, grandma's face in shadow on the pillow
shots.hero: Pillow, grey hair, face mostly in shadow, two small eye highlights
shots.vo: Don't look. She's just checking on me.

shots.hero: Ward in pale morning light, narrator asleep in the chair
shots.vo: So I didn't. I stared at the ceiling until morning.

shots.hero: A fresh IV bag with a handwritten time label '02:00' and a long dark hair caught on the stand
shots.vo: The doctor asked who changed Grandma's IV at two a.m. No nurse was on that ward.

shots.framing: Low angle, floor beside the bed
shots.hero: A faint smeared trail on the tiles leading under the curtain
shots.vo: And on the floor, a trail. Like someone had dragged themselves away.

shots.hero: CTA with a nurse cap / floor tile motif

shots.framing: Wide, empty street, one streetlight, a tall figure under it
shots.hero: Tall masked woman in a trench coat standing perfectly still under the streetlight
shots.vo: In Japan, if a woman in a mask stops you at night and asks if she's pretty… don't say yes. Or no.

shots.hero: Title 'KUCHISAKE-ONNA' + '口裂け女 · Japan' over a masked silhouette in profile
shots.vo: They call her Kuchisake-onna. The slit-mouthed woman.

shots.hero: A white surgical mask held by long pale fingers, its ear loop slowly slipping
shots.vo: Say no, and she takes you. Say yes… and she takes off the mask.

shots.hero: Schoolgirl with a school bag walking toward the streetlight
shots.vo: My sister walked home from cram school every night. Past the same streetlight.

shots.framing: Wide, the woman appears under the light
shots.hero: The tall masked woman under the light, the small schoolgirl stopped in the foreground
shots.vo: One night, a very tall woman in a long coat was standing under it. Wearing a mask.

shots.framing: Low angle, the woman leaning down
shots.hero: The masked face leaning down into frame from above, hair hanging, eyes shadowed
shots.vo: She leaned down, close to my sister's face…

shots.framing: Extreme close, the mask and eyes
shots.hero: Mask edge and two dark eyes under a black fringe, mask slightly tugging as she speaks
shots.vo: Am I pretty?

shots.framing: Close, the sister's hands gripping her bag strap
shots.hero: Two small hands gripping a school bag strap, knuckles pale
shots.vo: My sister remembered what Grandma told her. Never yes. Never no.

shots.hero: Schoolgirl's profile silhouette looking up, breath visible
shots.vo: She said, 'You look… average.'

shots.framing: Wide, the woman frozen, the girl running
shots.hero: Woman motionless under the light, schoolgirl running away toward camera
shots.vo: The woman froze. Confused. And my sister ran.

shots.framing: Wide, the empty street, the light flickering
shots.hero: Empty street under the light; on the ground, a dropped white mask
shots.vo: She made it home. She never took that street again.

shots.framing: Medium, our front gate at night
shots.hero: A family house gate with a nameplate, a tall masked shadow cast across it
shots.vo: But last week, a tall woman in a mask asked me for directions… to our house.

shots.hero: CTA with a surgical mask motif

shots.hero: A small white kneeling figure far away at the water's edge, moon reflection
shots.vo: In Mexico, if you hear a woman crying by the river at night… walk away. Don't help her.

shots.hero: Title 'LA LLORONA' + 'The weeping woman · Mexico' over a veiled woman in white
shots.vo: They call her La Llorona. The weeping woman.

shots.hero: Two small paper boats drifting on dark water, one tipping over

shots.framing: Medium, boy sneaking to the river
shots.hero: Boy with fishing rod and flashlight walking through reeds
shots.vo: When my cousin was ten, he snuck out to fish at night.

shots.framing: Wide, the woman kneeling by the water
shots.hero: Woman in white kneeling at the edge, the boy small in the foreground reeds
shots.vo: He heard crying. A woman in a white dress, kneeling by the water.

shots.framing: Close, her hands in the river
shots.hero: Pale hands moving under the dark water surface, ripples, moon glints
shots.vo: Her hands were searching the river. Again and again.

shots.framing: Close, her veiled face, hair dripping
shots.hero: Long wet hair hanging over a pale face, water dripping, face not visible
shots.vo: Where are my children?

shots.hero: Boy's flashlight beam on the white figure, her head starting to turn
shots.vo: He stepped closer to help. And she stopped crying.

shots.hero: Boy running up the bank, flashlight beam swinging, the white figure standing up behind

shots.framing: Low angle, wet footprints on the floor

shots.hero: Wooden windowsill with a long wet black hair and a few drops of water

shots.framing: Wide, the river at night again

shots.hero: CTA with a marigold and river-ripple motif
shots.vo: Would you help her? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, dark pine trail at night

shots.vo: In South Korea, if you hear your mother calling you from the mountain… don't answer.

shots.hero: Title 'THE JANGSAN TIGER' + '장산범 · Busan' over a huge pale silhouette between pines
shots.vo: They call it the Jangsan Tiger.

shots.hero: A single long tuft of white fur caught on a pine branch, snow falling

shots.framing: Wide, apartment block at the foot of the mountain
shots.hero: Apartment block with a few lit windows, dark mountain looming behind

shots.hero: Friend's silhouette at a dark window, the pine trail visible outside
shots.vo: One night, she heard her mother's voice calling her name… from the trail outside.

shots.hero: Warm kitchen doorway, mother in an apron standing very still, looking at the window

shots.framing: Close, a hand on her shoulder
shots.hero: An adult hand on a sweater shoulder, the window glow beyond
shots.vo: Her mother put a hand on her shoulder and whispered…

shots.hero: Mother's profile in half shadow, eyes on the window

shots.hero: Dark window glass with the friend's faint reflection; outside, two dull eyes between pines

shots.framing: Wide, the apartment from outside, lights going off

shots.vo: They shut every window and waited for dawn.

shots.framing: Low angle, giant tracks in the snow

shots.hero: Pine trail at dusk, a faint pale shape waiting far up

shots.hero: CTA with a pine and white-fur motif

shots.hero: A fingertip trace in mirror fog slowly filling in by itself

shots.hero: Three girls in pyjamas on sleeping bags, string lights, one flashlight

shots.hero: Three silhouettes walking down a dark hallway toward a door, the candle glow on them

shots.framing: Medium, three girls before the mirror

shots.hero: The reflection's face in shadow, eyes open a beat too long

shots.framing: Close, a pale shape behind the reflection
shots.hero: Behind the girl's reflection, a blurred pale shape with long dark hair, very faint
shots.vo: Then, behind it, something pale smiled.

shots.framing: Wide, the bathroom door from the hallway
shots.hero: Bathroom door ajar, a sliver of candle light, the hallway empty
shots.vo: I ran. I never told my friends. We never played it again.

shots.hero: A clean mirror in morning light; the reflection's eyes still a little too dark
shots.vo: But every morning, in the mirror… I wait for my reflection to blink first.

shots.hero: CTA with a candle and mirror-fog motif
shots.vo: Would you say it three times? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, a small kampung shop at night, one bulb
shots.hero: A tiny bald silhouette slipping under the shop's shutters
shots.vo: In Indonesia, if your money keeps disappearing at night… put a bowl of water with a crab by the door.

shots.hero: Title 'TUYUL' + 'An Indonesian legend' over a tiny bald silhouette holding a coin
shots.vo: Because you might have a tuyul.

shots.hero: A few coins and a toy marble rolling on a wooden floor
shots.vo: A small spirit that steals money for its master. But it can't resist playing.

shots.framing: Medium, uncle counting money at the counter
shots.hero: Uncle at the wooden counter counting coins into a tin under the bulb
shots.vo: My uncle runs a small shop. Every night, he counted the money. Every morning, some was gone.

shots.hero: A closed money tin with a padlock, a few coins beside it
shots.vo: The tin was locked. The windows were shut. But the coins kept vanishing.

shots.framing: Close, the bowl with a crab by the door
shots.hero: Clay bowl of water on the floor by the door, a small red crab inside
shots.vo: So Grandma told him: put a crab in a bowl of water by the door.

shots.framing: Wide, the dark shop at night
shots.hero: Dark shop interior, the bowl by the door glinting, uncle's eyes peeking above the counter
shots.vo: That night, he hid behind the counter and waited.

shots.hero: Water in the bowl rippling, the crab moving, a small grey hand reaching in
shots.vo: At three a.m., he heard tiny footsteps. Then… splashing.

shots.framing: Close, the small hand and the crab
shots.hero: Small grey child-like hand poking the crab, droplets
shots.vo: Something small was playing with the crab. Giggling. All night long.

shots.hero: Morning light through the shutters, the bowl, puddles on the floor
shots.vo: By morning, not a single coin was missing. But the floor was wet.

shots.hero: Small child footprints circling the bowl and leading under the door
shots.vo: Tiny wet footprints. Going round and round the bowl. And then… out under the door.

shots.framing: Medium, uncle at the counter at night again
shots.hero: Uncle looking at the empty bowl by the door under the bulb
shots.vo: He still keeps the bowl there. Because last night… the crab was gone.

shots.hero: CTA with a coin and crab motif
shots.vo: Would you try the crab trick? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, stilt house over the canal at night
shots.hero: A teak stilt house over dark water, one lamp in the window
shots.vo: In Thailand, if someone you love reaches for something that fell… and their arm keeps going… don't let them know you saw.

shots.hero: Title 'MAE NAK' + 'แม่นาก · Thailand' over a woman's silhouette with long hair in lamp light
shots.vo: This is the story of Mae Nak.

shots.hero: An oil lamp still burning on a windowsill, a wilted jasmine garland beside it
shots.vo: A young wife who waited for her husband to come home from war. She waited… even after she died.

shots.hero: Man stepping from a small boat to the house steps; a woman silhouette with a bundle waiting in the doorway
shots.vo: When her husband came back, she was there. Smiling. With their baby in her arms.

shots.framing: Medium, the couple inside, lamp light
shots.hero: Inside: the wife preparing food at a low table, the husband sitting, warm lamp
shots.vo: The neighbors stopped visiting. They tried to warn him. He didn't listen.

shots.framing: Close, a lime rolling across the floor
shots.hero: A green lime rolling across teak floorboards toward a gap
shots.vo: One evening, she was making chili paste. A lime rolled off the table…

shots.framing: Close, the lime falling through the gap

shots.vo: …and fell through the floorboards, to the ground below.

shots.framing: Wide, under the house from outside
shots.hero: Husband under the stilt house by the boat, looking up; a pale hand emerging between boards above
shots.vo: He was underneath, fixing the boat. He saw a hand come through the floor.

shots.framing: Low angle, the arm stretching down

shots.hero: An impossibly long thin pale arm reaching down from the floorboards to the lime on the ground
shots.vo: And the arm kept stretching. Down. Down. Two meters. To pick up the lime.

shots.framing: Medium, husband frozen in the dark
shots.hero: Husband climbing the steps, the wife's silhouette in the lamp-lit door
shots.vo: He didn't scream. He just went back upstairs. And smiled at his wife.

shots.framing: Wide, the canal at night, a figure running
shots.hero: Tiny figure running along the canal bank away from the house; the window lamp still on
shots.vo: That night, he told her he was going to the toilet. And he ran.

shots.framing: Close, the lamp in the window
shots.hero: The oil lamp in the window, a long shadow of hair moving behind it
shots.vo: They say she's still waiting by the lamp. For him to come back.

shots.hero: CTA with a lime and lamp motif
shots.vo: Would you have run? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, wet country lane at night
shots.hero: A silver comb glinting in a puddle on a dark lane between stone walls
shots.vo: In Ireland, if you find a silver comb on the road… don't pick it up.

shots.hero: Title 'THE BANSHEE' + 'Bean sí · Ireland' over a pale woman with long white hair in mist
shots.vo: It belongs to the banshee.

shots.hero: A long white hair strand caught in the teeth of a silver comb

shots.framing: Medium, a girl walking home in the rain
shots.hero: Girl in a raincoat bending toward the comb on the lane

shots.framing: Close, the comb on the kitchen table
shots.hero: The silver comb on a wooden table by the fire, an old man's hand stopping mid-reach

shots.hero: Old man in a wool cap pointing to the dark window; the girl holding the comb
shots.vo: 'Put it on the windowsill,' he said. 'Now.'

shots.hero: Lit cottage in the rain; a pale grey figure far away by the stone wall
shots.vo: At midnight, we heard it. A woman wailing outside. Coming closer.

shots.framing: Close, the window, rain on the glass
shots.hero: Rain-streaked window, the comb on the sill inside, a long pale hand rising outside the glass
shots.vo: Then a long pale hand reached up to the window.

shots.hero: Empty windowsill, latch closed, a single long white hair on the wood
shots.vo: In the morning, the comb was gone. The window was still locked.

shots.hero: Old man in his chair by the fire, calm
shots.vo: My grandfather smiled. 'She only wanted it back,' he said.

shots.hero: Small group of mourners at a stone churchyard in grey dawn, a pale figure far on the hill
shots.vo: He passed away that winter. Peacefully. And at his funeral… I heard her wail once.

shots.framing: Close, a silver comb in a puddle again
shots.hero: A silver comb in a puddle on a suburban road at night
shots.vo: Last week, I found another comb. On my road.

shots.hero: CTA with a silver comb and rain motif
shots.vo: Would you pick it up? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Medium, inside a lit elevator alone
shots.hero: Narrator from behind facing closed steel doors, floor panel glowing
shots.vo: In Korea, if you play the elevator game… and a woman gets on at the fifth floor… don't look at her. Don't speak.

shots.hero: Title 'THE ELEVATOR GAME' + '엘리베이터 게임 · Korea' over a floor-number panel
shots.vo: They call it the elevator game.

shots.hero: Floor buttons lighting up one by one in sequence: 4 2 6 2 10 5
shots.vo: Ride alone. Press four, two, six, two, ten. Then five. If it works, you reach another world.

shots.framing: Wide, empty apartment lobby at night
shots.hero: Empty lobby, elevator doors waiting, exit sign
shots.vo: At one a.m., I tried it. Alone. In my building's elevator.

shots.hero: A finger pressing lit buttons, the floor display changing
shots.vo: Four. Two. Six. Two. Ten. Every floor was empty.

shots.framing: Wide, the doors open on an empty hallway
shots.hero: From inside the lift: doors opening on a dim hallway; a woman with long black hair standing with her back turned
shots.vo: Then I pressed five. The doors opened.

shots.hero: Woman in a dark coat in the corner, long hair, back to camera; narrator's reflection in the steel
shots.vo: A woman got on. She stood in the corner. Facing the wall.

shots.hero: Panel numbers climbing past 6, 7, 8, 9
shots.vo: I pressed one, to go down. The elevator went up.

shots.framing: Close, the reflection in the steel doors
shots.hero: Blurred reflection in brushed steel: the woman's head turning, hair moving, no face
shots.vo: In the steel, I saw her reflection. She was slowly turning her head.

shots.framing: Close, a hand hitting the button
shots.hero: Hand slamming the button, doors opening, narrator bursting out
shots.vo: I hit ten. The doors opened. I ran.

shots.framing: Wide, stairwell, a figure running down
shots.hero: Concrete stairwell, narrator running down, exit sign glow
shots.vo: I took the stairs all the way down. I never looked back.

shots.framing: Wide, the lobby, the elevator doors closing
shots.hero: Lobby elevator open and lit, the panel showing 5, nobody inside
shots.vo: When I reached the lobby, the elevator was waiting. Doors open. Lit up. On five.

shots.hero: CTA with a floor-panel motif
shots.vo: Would you play it? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, a village house in the rain at night
shots.hero: A Javanese house with a lit porch; a tall man's silhouette standing at the gate in the rain
shots.vo: In Java, if your husband comes home early from the night shift… and won't say a word… check twice.

shots.hero: Title 'GENDERUWO' + 'A Javanese legend' over a tall hairy silhouette in a doorway
shots.vo: It might be a genderuwo.

shots.hero: A man's work jacket hanging on a hook, dripping, with long dark hairs on the shoulders
shots.vo: A spirit that can take the shape of someone you trust. It copies their face. But never their voice.

shots.framing: Medium, mother and daughter watching TV
shots.hero: Mother and daughter on a sofa in TV glow, rain on the window
shots.vo: My father works nights at the factory. It was just me and Mom, watching TV.

shots.hero: Front door opening, a tall man's silhouette in work clothes, soaking wet, face in shadow
shots.vo: At ten p.m., the front door opened. It was Dad.

shots.framing: Medium, he walks past without a word
shots.hero: The tall figure passing behind the sofa, ducking slightly under the doorframe, wet footprints
shots.vo: He didn't say hello. He walked straight to the bedroom. Dripping. Silent.

shots.framing: Close, mother's face in TV glow
shots.hero: Mother's profile lit by the TV, a phone lighting up on the cushion
shots.vo: Mom said he must be tired. Then her phone rang.

shots.hero: Phone screen showing an incoming call 'BAPAK' with a photo silhouette
shots.vo: The screen said: Dad.

shots.framing: Close, mother holding the phone to her ear
shots.hero: Mother's hand holding the phone to her ear, her eyes moving to the hallway
shots.vo: Hi. I'll be home late tonight. Lock the door.

shots.framing: Wide, the dark hallway to the bedroom
shots.hero: Dark hallway, the bedroom door creaking open, a tall shape in the dark
shots.vo: Mom looked at me. Then at the bedroom door. It was slowly opening.

shots.framing: Wide, mother and daughter running out in the rain
shots.hero: Two figures running across the yard in the rain, the house door open behind them
shots.vo: We ran out into the rain and didn't stop until the neighbors' house.

shots.hero: The house in grey dawn light, a man with a motorbike at the gate looking at the open door
shots.vo: When Dad got home at dawn, the bed was soaked. And full of long, black hair.

shots.hero: CTA with a phone and door motif
shots.vo: Would you have noticed? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, empty school corridor at dusk
shots.hero: Long empty corridor with sliding windows, sunset fading, the girls' bathroom sign at the end
shots.vo: In Japan, if the school bathroom is empty after class… never knock on the third stall.

shots.hero: Title 'HANAKO-SAN' + 'トイレの花子さん · Japan' over a stall door with the number 3
shots.vo: Someone might answer.

shots.hero: The hem of a red pleated skirt visible under a closed stall door
shots.vo: They call her Hanako-san. A girl in a red skirt who never left the third stall.

shots.framing: Medium, two schoolgirls in the corridor
shots.hero: Two schoolgirls with bags walking down the corridor at dusk, long shadows
shots.vo: After club practice, my friend and I were the last ones in the building.

shots.hero: Row of three stall doors, the third one closed, one fluorescent tube flickering
shots.vo: She dared me. Knock three times. Ask if Hanako is there.

shots.framing: Close, knuckles on the third door
shots.hero: A girl's knuckles knocking on the stall door marked 3
shots.vo: I knocked. One. Two. Three. 'Hanako-san… are you there?'

shots.framing: Medium, the two girls before the door
shots.hero: Two girls from behind facing the closed third door, one with a hand over her mouth
shots.vo: Silence. My friend laughed. Then, from inside… a small voice answered.

shots.framing: Close, the gap under the third door
shots.hero: Dark gap under the stall door; something red shifts in the shadow
shots.vo: Yes… I'm here.

shots.framing: Low angle, the door creeping open
shots.hero: The stall door opening a crack; a small red shoe on the tiles inside
shots.vo: The door began to open. Slowly. And I saw a small red shoe.

shots.framing: Medium, the girls running down the corridor
shots.hero: Two silhouettes running down the dark corridor toward the stairs
shots.vo: We ran. Down the hall, down the stairs, all the way outside.

shots.framing: Wide, the school building at night
shots.hero: The school building at night, one bathroom window faintly lit
shots.vo: The next day, I told our teacher. She went pale. 'That bathroom… only has two stalls.'

shots.framing: Wide, the bathroom with two stalls
shots.hero: Two stall doors and a bare tiled wall where a third should be, faint knuckle marks on the tiles
shots.vo: I went back. Two stalls. A blank wall where the third should be. And sometimes… it still knocks. Three times.

shots.hero: CTA with a stall door and red shoe motif
shots.vo: Would you knock? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, the plains under a huge moon
shots.hero: Endless grass plain under a huge moon, a lone palm, a tiny tall figure on the horizon
shots.vo: In Venezuela, if you hear a whistle at night… and it sounds far away… he is right beside you.

shots.hero: Title 'EL SILBÓN' + 'The Whistler · Venezuela' over a tall thin silhouette with a hat
shots.vo: They call him El Silbón.

shots.hero: Seven pale music notes rising over the grass; an old tied sack hanging from a long thin hand
shots.vo: A giant, thin wanderer of the plains. He whistles seven notes. And he carries a sack of bones.

shots.framing: Medium, ranch porch with a lantern
shots.hero: Grandfather on the porch with a lantern, two dogs cowering at his feet
shots.vo: My grandfather kept cattle on the plains. One night, the dogs started whining.

shots.hero: Wind moving through tall grass under the moon, nobody in sight
shots.vo: Then we heard it. Whistling. Do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, si.

shots.framing: Medium, the girl at the window
shots.hero: Girl at a shuttered window looking out at the moonlit plain
shots.vo: It sounded far away. Somewhere across the river.

shots.hero: Grandfather's hand on the girl's shoulder, both crouched below the window, lantern turned low
shots.vo: My grandfather pulled me down. 'If it sounds far,' he whispered, 'he's close.'

shots.framing: Close, the shutters, a long shadow outside
shots.hero: Moonlight through shutter slats; a very tall thin shadow falls across the floor
shots.vo: The whistling stopped. And right under the window… something dropped.

shots.framing: Close, the shadow on the wall
shots.hero: On the wall, the shadow of long fingers lifting small shapes from a sack
shots.vo: We heard bones rattling. Being counted. One by one.

shots.framing: Medium, grandfather opening the door at dawn
shots.hero: Grey dawn light spilling through the opening door, grandfather's silhouette
shots.vo: My grandfather didn't move until the rooster crowed. Then he opened the door.

shots.framing: Wide, footprints leading away at dawn
shots.hero: A line of very long thin footprints leading from the porch into the misty grass
shots.vo: In the dust: footprints. Long. Thin. Barefoot. Walking away across the plains.

shots.framing: Close, the window at night again
shots.hero: Apartment window at night, city lights, the curtain stirring
shots.vo: Last night, in the city, I heard a whistle. Very, very far away.

shots.hero: CTA with a hat silhouette and music-note motif
shots.vo: Would you look out the window? Comment YES or NO.

shots.hero: Stilt huts among palms under the moon, one window lit
shots.vo: In the Philippines, if a stranger moves into your village… look into their eyes. If your reflection is upside down… run.

shots.hero: Title 'ASWANG' + 'A Philippine legend' over a large black bird shape on a thatched roof
shots.vo: It might be an aswang.

shots.hero: A capiz window at night, a huge wing shadow passing over it
shots.vo: A shapeshifter. Kind by day. Hungry at night. And it loves the smell of a new baby.

shots.framing: Medium, the neighbor visiting the baby
shots.hero: Mother holding a swaddled baby, a smiling woman neighbor offering a dish, lamp light
shots.vo: When my brother was born, a new neighbor came to visit. She was so kind.

shots.framing: Close, garlic and salt by the door
shots.hero: Garlic bulbs hanging from a window frame, a bowl of salt on the threshold
shots.vo: Lola didn't trust her. She hung garlic by the window. And salt by the door.

shots.framing: Medium, Lola whispering to the girl
shots.hero: Lola beside the girl, both watching the neighbor lean over the crib
shots.vo: When the neighbor leaned over the crib, Lola whispered: 'Look at her eyes.'

shots.hero: A woman's eye in lamp light; in the iris, a tiny reflection of the girl, upside down
shots.vo: In her eyes, I saw myself. Upside down.

shots.framing: Wide, a huge bird on the roof
shots.hero: The hut in moonlight, a huge black bird silhouette perched on the thatch
shots.vo: That night, something landed on our roof. Heavy. Like a giant bird.

shots.hero: Lola praying by the crib, lamp low, thatch above in shadow
shots.vo: Lola sat by the crib with her rosary. All night. Above us, the roof creaked.

shots.framing: Close, a gap in the thatch
shots.hero: Moonlit gap in the thatch above the crib, a dark shape shifting behind it
shots.vo: Something sniffed through the gaps in the roof. Slow. Hungry.

shots.framing: Wide, the neighbor's hut at dawn
shots.hero: Empty hut in grey dawn, black feathers scattered on the bamboo steps
shots.vo: At dawn, the neighbor's house was empty. Only black feathers on the steps.

shots.framing: Close, a smiling stranger, lamp light
shots.hero: A friendly woman's face in soft light, her eye catching a tiny inverted reflection
shots.vo: Years later, a new neighbor smiled at me. And in her eyes… I was upside down.

shots.hero: CTA with garlic and feather motif
shots.vo: Would you look into her eyes? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, four teens in a candle circle
shots.hero: Four teens sitting in a circle on a bedroom floor around candles, a small doll in the middle
shots.vo: In Indonesia, if you call a spirit with a jelangkung… you must send it back before midnight.

shots.hero: Title 'JELANGKUNG' + 'An Indonesian legend' over the doll's silhouette
shots.vo: Or it stays.

shots.hero: The coconut-shell doll in faded cloth, a pencil tied beneath it touching paper
shots.vo: A doll made from a coconut shell and a stick. Hold it over paper… and a spirit writes.

shots.framing: Medium, hands joining around the doll
shots.hero: Four pairs of hands holding the doll's stick over a sheet of paper
shots.vo: Four of us tried it in my friend's room. Candles. Paper. And the old chant: come uninvited… leave unescorted.

shots.hero: The tied pencil dragging a shaky line on the paper
shots.vo: The doll got heavy. Then the pencil started to move.

shots.hero: Paper covered in the scrawled word PLAY repeated
shots.vo: It wrote one word. Over and over. PLAY.

shots.framing: Medium, the teens laughing, candles low
shots.hero: Teens laughing in the circle, candles burned low
shots.vo: We laughed. We asked silly questions. We lost track of time.

shots.hero: A wall clock showing 12:01, candle light on its face
shots.vo: Then my friend looked at the clock. Twelve-oh-one. Midnight.

shots.hero: The pencil pressing hard, writing NO, the paper tearing
shots.vo: We begged it to go home. The pencil wrote: NO.

shots.hero: Dark room lit only by the window, smoke from the candles, a shadow on the wall that matches no one
shots.vo: We dropped the doll. Every candle went out. And something laughed in the dark.

shots.hero: Grey dawn in the room, burnt-out candles, an empty space where the doll was
shots.vo: In the morning, the doll was gone. We searched everywhere. We never found it.

shots.framing: Close, a homework page at midnight
shots.hero: A school notebook under a desk lamp, one scrawled word PLAY at the bottom of the page
shots.vo: But every night at midnight, my homework has one new word. In pencil. PLAY.

shots.hero: CTA with the doll and a pencil motif
shots.vo: Would you play jelangkung? Comment YES or NO.

shots.framing: Wide, a misty loch at dusk
shots.hero: Still loch at dusk, mist, hills; a black horse standing in the shallows
shots.vo: In Scotland, if a black horse waits by the loch… and lets you touch it… don't. Your hand will stick.

shots.hero: Title 'THE KELPIE' + 'A Scottish legend' over a horse head silhouette with a dripping mane
shots.vo: It's a kelpie.

shots.hero: A dripping black mane tangled with water weed, drops falling
shots.vo: A water horse with a dripping mane. It lets children climb on… then runs into the water.

shots.framing: Medium, two kids on the shore path
shots.hero: A girl and a small boy in wellies on a stone path by the water
shots.vo: My little brother and I were walking home along the loch at dusk.

shots.framing: Wide, the horse in the shallows
shots.hero: The black horse standing in still water, its reflection, mist around its legs
shots.vo: A black horse stood in the shallows. No saddle. No rider. Just waiting.

shots.framing: Close, the wet mane and a small hand
shots.hero: Dripping mane with weed, a small hand reaching toward it
shots.vo: Its mane was wet. Tangled with weeds. My brother reached out to pet it.

shots.framing: Close, the hand on the hide
shots.hero: A small hand pressed flat on glistening black hide, fingers unable to lift
shots.vo: His hand touched its neck. And it stuck.

shots.framing: Wide, the horse turning toward the water
shots.hero: Horse stepping deeper into the water, the boy pulled along at its side
shots.vo: The horse turned toward the loch. And started walking.

shots.framing: Close, the girl's hand in her pocket
shots.hero: The girl's hand pulling an old iron key from her coat pocket
shots.vo: I grabbed his other arm. Grandma always said: iron breaks the spell.

shots.framing: Close, the iron key on the hide
shots.hero: An old iron key pressed against wet black hide, steam curling
shots.vo: I pressed our old iron key against its neck.

shots.framing: Wide, the horse vanishing into the loch
shots.hero: Two kids on the shore, the loch perfectly still where the horse was, mist
shots.vo: It shrieked. My brother fell free. And the horse sank into the loch without a ripple.

shots.framing: Wide, a garden at night by the cottage
shots.hero: A cottage garden at night, the lit window, a dark dripping horse by the far gate
shots.vo: We never told anyone. But some evenings… a wet black horse stands at the end of our garden.

shots.hero: CTA with a mane and iron key motif
shots.vo: Would you have touched it? Comment YES or NO.
